VIVARIUM — DESIGN MARKUPS
What to cut, what to add. Left column is the app as it is today, recreated from src/. Right column is the proposal. Both at 390px.

CUT — delete it. The information is duplicated, or it does not change what you do next.
MERGE / TRIM / SWAP — keep the information, spend less screen on it.
NEW — add it. In every case here the data already exists in the app and never reaches a screen.

The thread running through all three screens: the app tells you a lot about state, and very little about what to do about it — and it tells you the same state three or four times per screen.

The second page, Mobile vs web, takes this proposal to 1440px.

DASHBOARD

Cut
· "Fed this week" stat card — punishes long feeding cycles
· The whole-collection photo grid — it is the Animals tab, and it renders every animal
· The three mini stats at the bottom — all three live on Stats

Merge
· "Needs feeding" + "Due soon" → one queue ordered by lateness

Add
· A workload line under the greeting
· Last meal on each queue row, so Feed can prefill
· Medication doses in the queue — medication_schedules is modelled and never rendered
· Select → batch log for the queue
· Low feeder stock, before you start feeding

Net: roughly 1720px of scroll down to about 1280, and the part you act on fits on one screen.

ANIMALS

Cut
· The urgent carousel — the third rendering of the overdue list, sitting on top of the search box
· Streak badge and tag chips on the card

Change
· "Fed 18 days ago" → "4 days overdue". 18 days is fine for one animal and late for another; only the schedule knows which.

Add
· Status filter chips — you can sort by overdue today, but not filter to it, and quarantine is invisible
· Grid / list density toggle — the photo grid is lovely at 12 animals and unusable at 50
· Enclosure on the card

Open question: is the Enclosures tab pulling its weight where it is, or is it really a grouping of this list?

ANIMAL PROFILE

This screen states "this animal is late" three times in the top 400px: the header chip, the banner, and the Next feeding tile.

Cut
· The header chip row — all three chips repeat the stats grid below, with less in them
· The overdue banner
· Two tabs: Feeding and Vitals are Timeline with a filter chip pre-selected

Add
· One feeding bar carrying status + last meal + the only Feed button
· Enclosure under the name
· "Takes food — 9 of 10", already computed on the Feeding tab, promoted to a tile
· Weight sparkline on its tile
· Health as the third quick action

Nothing is deleted from the data — the Feeding and Vitals tabs' contents are already reachable through Timeline's filters.

MOBILE VS WEB
The same proposal at 1440px, and the rules that get it there.

What exists today: the app's whole responsive treatment is four things — card grids go 2 → 3 → 4 columns, the bottom padding drops (md:pb-8, in six files), the FAB hides, and the sidebar appears. Grep the pages and you find seven breakpoint utilities in Dashboard, seven in AnimalDetail, five in Animals, and one each everywhere else. There is no desktop layout; there is a phone layout centred in a max-w-5xl column with 96px of dead gutter on each side.

The answer is not a separate web design — it is one set of components that know what to do with more width. The first board shows the problem, the next two show the proposal, and the last one is the spec.

TODAY AT 1440px

Three things break, and none of them are cosmetic.

1. Rows stretch instead of filling. A queue row spans 1024px with a 10px dot at one end and a 12px button at the other. The fields that would justify that width — the schedule, the last meal, the enclosure — are not shown at any width.

2. The stat grid is grid-cols-2 with no breakpoint at all: two 506px cards, each holding a single digit.

3. Four actions disappear. The FAB offers add animal, feeding, shed, weight and expense; it is md:hidden, and its desktop replacement is one Log feeding button. Above 768px, logging a shed or a weight means opening an animal first.

The photo grid is the one thing that genuinely responds.

WEB DASHBOARD

The phone's three blocks, reordered rather than redesigned.

· The queue keeps the primary column and unfolds: status, last meal and location come out from under the name into their own columns. Below 1024 they fold back into the two-line mobile row. One component, two arrangements.

· Stock and activity — read often, acted on rarely — move into a 380px rail instead of sitting below the fold.

· The FAB becomes a split button carrying the same five actions in the same order, opening the same modals.

· Content caps at 1240px so a wide monitor grows the gutters, not the rows.

Same 40–44px targets as the phone. A mouse tolerates smaller buttons; it does not earn them.

WEB ANIMAL PROFILE

The mobile profile is a vertical stack: hero, identity, feeding bar, quick actions, stats, then tabs. On desktop that entire stack becomes a 380px rail, pinned, and the tab content fills the rest — so the animal stays on screen while you read six months of its history.

The payoff is the records. Every feeding row stores prey, size, quantity, refusal, notes and who logged it; the phone can show two of those. Desktop is where you audit a season, so desktop is where the columns appear.

Same for the growth chart: a sparkline in the Weight tile on a phone, the real chart inline on the web. Recharts is already a dependency.

Note the profile is capped at max-w-3xl today — 768px on a 1440px screen.
